title: Choosing evenweave and linen for cross-stitch
subtitle: The alternatives to Aida for finer, more flexible work
excerpt: Evenweave and linen offer an alternative to Aida for cross-stitch. Both have individual threads rather than grouped blocks, so each stitch is worked over two threads rather than one Aida square. The result is a softer, more fabric-like finish at higher thread counts. 28-count evenweave stitched over two threads gives the same stitch size as 14-count Aida.
sourceNotes: Evenweave and linen specifications from manufacturer technical literature. The over-two-threads convention for counted cross-stitch on evenweave is documented in all major UK cross-stitch publications.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fabric woven with individual threads of equal weight in both directions, unlike Aida's grouped thread blocks. Cross-stitch on evenweave is worked over two threads in each direction, so a 28-count evenweave gives the same stitch size as 14-count Aida. The surface has a softer, more fabric-like texture than Aida.

The visual difference is in the background. Aida shows a clear grid between the filled squares; evenweave and linen show a smoother, more continuous fabric surface around the stitches. For pieces that will be left partially unstitched, evenweave often looks more refined.
Equivalent to 11-count Aida. Chunky stitches, very visible grid. Beginner-friendly on evenweave.
Equivalent to 14-count Aida. The standard evenweave count. Size 24 tapestry needle, two strands of floss.
Equivalent to 16-count Aida. Fine work. The linen weave has a natural slub that makes the fabric surface slightly irregular. Size 26 needle, two strands.
Equivalent to 18-count Aida. Very fine work. One strand for most stitching. Magnification essential.

On evenweave, the needle enters and exits between pairs of threads rather than at Aida block corners. Count two threads across and two threads down to find each stitch corner. The movement is the same as on Aida; only the counting changes. Mark the counting grid with a water-erasable pen before beginning if the thread intersections are hard to see.
